newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: INSIGHT-AUSTRALIAN BONDS BRACED FOR KEY JOBS TEST.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT-AUSTRALIAN BONDS BRACED FOR KEY JOBS TEST.

text.p: *The Australian 10-year bond futures contract struggled back above the psychological 93.500 level in after hours trading as it braced itself for this week's key local data.
*Local July labour force data due at 11.30 a.m. (0130 GMT).
The September Australian 10-year bond futures contract struggled back above the psychological 93.500 level in after hours trading as it braced itself for this week's key local data.
The contract ended SYCOM at 93.520, but has yet to make a decisive clearance of the 93.500/93.510 area to suggest that the market can rally back to last week's 93.695 all time high.

Modest price gains in U.S. Treasuries on Wednesday helped to underpin the local move, but the domestic market will finally divert its attention away from the U.S. and the quarterly refunding auctions when the July labour force data is released.

The data, due at 11.30 a.m. (0130 GMT), has been keenly awaited since last week's monetary policy easing by the Reserve Bank as it may provide a clue as to whether another rate cut is on the agenda or whether policy will be on hold for sometime.

The reaction to the report will be notable at the short end and where bill futures have been trading at a modest discount to the new 5.0 percent official rate since the RBA annouced the rate cut last Wednesday.
Median expectations centre on a 25,000 rise in employment after the small 11,900 increase in June, while the unemployment rate is forecast at 8.6 percent against 8.5 percent previously.
The U.S. market closed steady as it awaited the third and final leg of the quarterly refunding auctions and despite a disappointing reception to Wednesday's 10-year note sale.
The US$10 billion 30-year bond auction is due later on Thursday.
